question: T4-58
answer:
## Reactor selection — Lumenford Bay series, 400 V / 50 Hz feeder, 75 kVA at 0.8 pf lagging

### 1. Data source and basis
Only the Lumenford Bay reactor catalogue (table T4-58-1) is used; no other vendor data, no derating factors. Catalogue definitions applied verbatim:
- `x` is the per-unit reactance on a base of **100 kVA at rated voltage**.
- Winding resistance is negligible (so the reactor impedance is purely reactive, Z = jX).
- Rated current is the continuous line current.

All four Bay models are rated 400 V, 50 Hz:

| Model | V rated | f rated | I rated (A) | kVA | x | Price (EUR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B-160 | 400 | 50 | 230.9 | 160 | 0.080 | 2000 |
| B-200 | 400 | 50 | 288.7 | 200 | 0.075 | 2800 |
| B-320 | 400 | 50 | 461.9 | 320 | 0.055 | 4500 |
| B-500 | 400 | 50 | 721.7 | 500 | 0.040 | 6100 |

### 2. Load current
S = 75 kVA, cos φ = 0.8 lagging → P = 60 kW, Q = 45 kvar.

Three-phase, 400 V line-to-line:

    I_load = S / (√3 · V_LL) = 75 000 / (1.732051 · 400) = 108.25 A  →  108.3 A

Cross-check through real power: I = P / (√3 · V_LL · cos φ) = 60 000 / (1.732051 · 400 · 0.8) = 108.25 A ✓

Required rated current ≥ 108.3 A. All four models satisfy this (smallest is 230.9 A).

### 3. Reactance conversion from the catalogue per-unit base
Base impedance of the catalogue base (100 kVA at rated voltage 400 V):

    Z_base = V_rated² / S_base = 400² / 100 000 = 1.600 Ω   (per phase: 230.94² / 33 333 = 1.600 Ω, identical)

    X = x · Z_base

Equivalent base current: I_base = S_base / (√3 · V_rated) = 100 000 / (1.732051 · 400) = 144.34 A.
The load therefore sits at I_load / I_base = 108.25 / 144.34 = 0.750 pu (equivalently 75 kVA / 100 kVA = 0.75).

### 4. Voltage drop through the reactor at load current
Definition used: the drop is the voltage appearing across the series reactor at the load current, ΔV = I_load · X (per phase), resistance neglected as stated in the catalogue. It is expressed as a percentage of rated voltage; the per-phase and line-to-line ratios are identical (√3 cancels):

    ΔV% = 100 · (I_load · X) / (400/√3) = 100 · x · (I_load / I_base) = 100 · x · 0.750

| Model | x | X = 1.6·x (Ω) | ΔV per phase (V) | ΔV line-line (V) | ΔV (% of 400 V) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B-160 | 0.080 | 0.1280 | 13.86 | 24.0 | 6.000 |
| B-200 | 0.075 | 0.1200 | 12.99 | 22.5 | 5.625 |
| B-320 | 0.055 | 0.0880 | 9.53 | 16.5 | 4.125 |
| B-500 | 0.040 | 0.0640 | 6.93 | 12.0 | 3.000 |

Worked check for B-500: X = 0.040 × 1.6 = 0.0640 Ω; ΔV = 108.253 × 0.0640 = 6.928 V per phase = 12.00 V line-to-line; 12.00 / 400 = 3.000 %.

### 5. Constraint screening (Bay catalogue only)

| Model | V_rated ≥ 380 V | f_rated ≥ 50 Hz | I_rated ≥ 108.3 A | Drop ≤ 3.0 % | Price (EUR) | Qualifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| B-160 | 400 ✓ | 50 ✓ | 230.9 ✓ | 6.000 ✗ | 2000 | No |
| B-200 | 400 ✓ | 50 ✓ | 288.7 ✓ | 5.625 ✗ | 2800 | No |
| B-320 | 400 ✓ | 50 ✓ | 461.9 ✓ | 4.125 ✗ | 4500 | No |
| B-500 | 400 ✓ | 50 ✓ | 721.7 ✓ | 3.000 ✓ | 6100 | Yes |

The voltage, frequency and current constraints are met by every model; the 3.0 % drop limit alone eliminates B-160, B-200 and B-320. B-500 is the only qualifying model and therefore the cheapest qualifying model by elimination — the low-price models cannot be used at this load regardless of their price, because their higher per-unit reactance produces 4.13 % to 6.00 % drop at 108.3 A.

### 6. Selected reactor — B-500
- Voltage drop at 108.3 A: 6.93 V per phase / 12.0 V line-to-line = **3.00 % of 400 V**, which does not exceed the 3.0 % limit (equal to it; the limit is stated as "shall not exceed").
- Rated current 721.7 A ≥ load current 108.3 A (margin 6.67×); rated kVA 500 vs 75 kVA load.
- Rated voltage 400 V ≥ 380 V; rated frequency 50 Hz ≥ 50 Hz.
- Price EUR 6100 (catalogue T4-58-1).

### Results

| | |
|---|---|
| Reactor | B-500 |
| Voltage drop (%) | 3.00 |
| Current (A) | 108.3 |
| Price (EUR) | 6100 |
